clue.text: Complete rest period for Americans

parts.note: complete or entire means full
a rest or halt is a stop

explanation.surface: A total holiday break, described as Americans might describe it.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English the punctuation mark Britons call a full stop is called a period, so the definition hangs on that transatlantic difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym across dialects: the dot ending a sentence is a period in American English.

clue.text: On the air, weird protagonist lacking traditional virtues

indicators.note: weird means strange or out of shape, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcast drama whose central figure is a strange, unheroic sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges ONTHEAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary term: a central character who lacks courage, nobility or other classic heroic qualities.

clue.text: Track record originally set by champion, programme reveals

indicators.note: set by means placed next to, so the following piece sits beside the first
originally means at the start, so take the first letter of record

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert
a course is a programme of study or treatment

explanation.surface: A sporting venue whose programme reveals a record set by a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals' is just a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a horse-racing venue is often called a track.

clue.text: Put right about item?

parts.note: re is a short word for about or concerning
a couple who are an item form a pair

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about fixing something regarding an object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item' in the sense of a romantic couple is the trick: a couple who are an item are a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mend or fix a thing is to put it right.

clue.text: Pitch players used

definitions.meaning: to pitch a ball or a line is to throw it
the actors in a production are its company of players

explanation.surface: Musical pitch and the instrumentalists who used it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: throw something, and the full list of actors in a show.

clue.text: Is the old lady after cleaner that shows pulling power?

indicators.note: after means the following words come behind the cleaner

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner
the old lady is slang for one's mother, ma

explanation.surface: Asking whether mother, following the cleaner, displays magnetic appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British term for a woman paid to clean a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who draws people to them has pulling power, a compelling personal magnetism.

clue.text: Resembling a big animal from island nursed by remarkable nurse

indicators.note: being nursed by means being held inside, so one piece goes within the other
remarkable read as re-markable, able to be marked differently, so the letters of nurse are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual nurse tending an islander who looks like a large beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges NURSE into URSNE, and 'nursed by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoological adjective: bear-like, from Latin ursus, the big animal meant here.

clue.text: Reason fool imprisoned by state

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to state is to say
a nit is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Sound logic suggests a fool is locked up by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a nation but is the verb meaning say.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reason in the sense of soundness of mind, one's wits.

clue.text: Sister crossing area by church in shade

indicators.note: by means next to, so the church follows
crossing means straddling, so the sister goes around the area

parts.note: a religious sister is a nun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun walks across a churchyard in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' as in a subtle shade of meaning, not shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a slight difference in tone, colour or meaning is a shade.

clue.text: Actress who played Norma Desmond — good in last performance

parts.note: Gloria Swanson played the faded star Norma Desmond in the film Sunset Boulevard

explanation.surface: A film star turning in a fine final appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a final public appearance or work, from the legend of a swan singing as it dies.

clue.text: Calling urgently about one petitioner

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: clamant means clamorous, insistently calling out
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lone petitioner loudly demanding attention.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAMANT is a rare word meaning noisy or urgently demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who lodges a claim or petition before a court or authority.

clue.text: Set on fire in the course of campaign, it exploded

indicators.note: in the course of means running through, so the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: During a military campaign a device blew up and lit a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to kindle or light something is to set it on fire.

clue.text: Soldiers initially observe German man breaking into military vehicles

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of observe
breaking into means entering, so the German man goes inside the vehicles

parts.note: tanks are armoured military vehicles
Herr is the German for Mr, a man

explanation.surface: Troops first spot a German forcing his way into armoured vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British army the other ranks are soldiers who are not commissioned officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Military term: the enlisted ranks below officers, the ordinary soldiers.

clue.text: Very much ungoverned, oddly defective

indicators.note: defective in its odd letters means the odd letters are missing, so keep the even ones

explanation.surface: Something enormously unruly, strangely faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of ungoverned leaves the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: no end means immensely, as in 'it pleased him no end'.

clue.text: In favour of person helping to produce rapid growth

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a life can mean a person, as in lives saved
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Backing someone who helps produce swift expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like an adjective describing the person but is a noun, a portion; 'to produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sudden rapid increase or spread in number is proliferation-style multiplication.

clue.text: In northern part of France, excavate beneath one

parts.note: in a down clue the northern part is the top, so the first three letters of France
to excavate is to dig

explanation.surface: Instructions to dig under something in the north of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beneath one' looks like an instruction to place letters but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase infra dignitatem: something below one's dignity, so beneath one.

clue.text: Not in good health? Corpulent editor may be unlucky

parts.note: someone not in good health is ill
corpulent means fat

explanation.surface: A sickly, overweight newspaper editor who might be doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: doomed or destined for misfortune, as an unlucky venture.

clue.text: Steep decline in doves flying close to shore

indicators.note: flying means scattered through the air, so the letters are rearranged
close to means the end of, so take the last letter of shore

explanation.surface: A sudden plunge among birds flying near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges INDOVES into NOSEDIV, then 'close to' adds E from shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor from aviation: a sudden steep drop, as in prices or fortunes.

clue.text: Wasted opening in board game

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A wasted opening move in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board game' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: wasted and blotto both mean very drunk.

clue.text: Over-the-top articles about Western capital

parts.note: OTT is the abbreviation for over the top

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles wrap the W

parts.note: A and A are two indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Excessive newspaper pieces written about a western city.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Heartless first leader disturbed one backing union of states

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged
heartless means losing the central letter of the word first

explanation.surface: An emotionally cold first head of state, upset, who backed a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes R from FIRST to leave FIST; 'disturbed' rearranges FIST and LEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: Political term: a supporter of federation, a union of states under a central government.

clue.text: Engineers are absent from being lax

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British army
to miss a class is to be absent from it

explanation.surface: Engineers skip work through being slack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: negligent or careless in one's duties.

clue.text: Unfortunate result for province

indicators.note: unfortunate means having bad luck, so the letters of result are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A bad outcome for a region.
explanation.walkthrough: ULSTER is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a province of Ireland, often used for Northern Ireland.

clue.text: One on raid given order before start of operation

indicators.note: before means the order comes ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a command is an order

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A raider receiving instructions before an operation begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a soldier trained for raids and assaults.

clue.text: One-roomed dwelling to dispose of, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so take a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: to sell something is to dispose of it

explanation.surface: A tiny one-room home somebody is said to want to get rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a monk's or prisoner's single small room.

clue.text: Sit astride and go off, following street on right

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the last piece sits behind the others

parts.note: eggs that go off or rot are said to addle

explanation.surface: Mount something with legs either side and leave, along a street to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' as in eggs going bad, not leaving; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sit or stand with a leg either side of something.

clue.text: Ballesteros catching the French liner

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the golfer's name goes around the article

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was a famous Spanish golfer
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A golfer catching a French ocean liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liner' suggests a ship but means a protective cover, such as a record sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sleeve is a tube-shaped cover or lining that something fits inside.

clue.text: Long leases arranged in US city

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lengthy property rentals organised in an American metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest city of California.
